title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Mike Vrabel considers keeping seven wide receivers on the New England Patriots roster for the upcoming NFL season.
The Patriots' wide receiver lineup includes A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism.
Kayshon Boutte is mentioned in trade rumors, while Kyle Williams is expected to play a significant role despite mixed camp performances.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates Kevin Hayden, Rachael Rollins, and Linda Champion debated ethics and leadership in Roxbury.
Rollins critiqued Hayden’s handling of gun violence and both faced questions on past ethics controversies.
Candidates discussed their visions for police accountability, with differing transparency proposals on body-camera footage.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Boston faces high humidity with pop-up storms possible Friday and Saturday evenings, according to the National Weather Service.
Temperatures near 90°F but feeling closer to 100°F are expected, with heat advisories in place for parts of southern New England.
Humidity will remain high through the weekend, gradually decreasing on Sunday into Monday with sticky conditions persisting.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: A Red Sox fan, Andy Zides, gifted Aroldis Chapman a vintage 1930s Bob Feller model glove before a game.
Chapman allowed a two-run home run during the game but the Red Sox won 12-11 in the 13th inning.
Chapman holds the record for fastest pitch at 105.8 MPH, a nod to Feller's reputation as an early flamethrower.

title: K-pop superstars BTS prepped for their Gillette shows at Planet Fitness in Downtown Crossing, apparently
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: BTS members Jung Hoseok, Kim Taehyung, and Jung Kook worked out at Planet Fitness in Downtown Crossing.
Jung Kook shared their gym visit on Instagram, catching public attention, especially from local BTS fans.
The unannounced visit to Planet Fitness occurred during BTS's sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium.

title: Meet Marty: Cape Cod’s newest great white shark is sticking around
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: The Atlantic White Shark Conservancy identified Marty, a new 10-foot great white shark off Cape Cod.
Since being tagged on July 16, Marty has pinged a receiver off North Truro 15 times, with data aiding research.
Stop & Shop celebrates the shark's identification by donating 20% of White Shark Marty plush toy sales to the conservancy.

title: 5 restaurants we can’t wait to try in August
author: Jillian Dara
bullets: About Thyme in Harvard Square offers Lebanese wraps and savory Middle Eastern flavors, opening in early August.
Tokyo-founded Nana's Green Tea serves matcha-based drinks and Japanese sweets on Newbury Street, now open.
Tom Yum Yang's new Allston location features Thai BBQ and street food, opening mid- to late-August.

title: Boston University joins growing list of colleges expanding financial aid
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston University will cap attendance costs at $20,000 annually for first-year students from families earning under $200,000.
Families earning $75,000 or less will pay nothing, with financial aid covering tuition, housing, and dining costs.
This initiative aligns with similar efforts by MIT, Harvard, and other institutions to expand need-based financial aid.

title: Mass. medical delivery worker charged after allegedly assaulting woman in wheelchair
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Qaisar Ali, 39, of Brockton, was arrested by East Bridgewater Police for allegedly assaulting a disabled woman in a wheelchair.
Ali faces charges including three counts of assault and battery on an elderly or disabled person and indecent exposure.
The alleged incident occurred during a pharmaceutical delivery, with Ali entering the home without consent and touching the woman.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial closes out second week after friends and former father-in-law testify
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial concluded its second week with testimonies from friends and former father-in-law.
Defense attorney accused prosecutors of inappropriate comments during medical testimony, leading to a tense courtroom exchange.
Witnesses described Clancy as a loving mother struggling with postpartum mental illness following the birth of her third child.
